title: Có sạc không?
summary: Different ways to say "Do you have a charger?" in Vietnam, with the phrase to start with, reusable pieces, and related next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Use this when you need any charger before you explain more detail. This is the quickest recovery phrase when the battery problem can be fixed nearby. Learn the full phrase first; the related phrases below help when the exchange moves one step further.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: This pattern turns the phrase into a yes-or-no question. Keep the main need together so the question stays natural.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Có sạc không? is the version to learn first for "Do you have a charger?". Use this when you need any charger before you explain more detail. If the person hesitates, show the place, object, or screen that gives the phrase context.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use this when you need any charger before you explain more detail. Use it in Wi-Fi, SIM, battery, charging, maps, and phone setup when one clear sentence will work better than a long explanation.

sections.title: Watch out
sections.body: Do not hand over your unlocked phone unless you trust the situation. Show the screen first.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Show the phone screen while you speak. A visible error message often explains the problem faster than more words.
